dedupe_keys.name: doe manufacturing energy and carbon footprints 2018 mecs

description: The Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints are diagrams that show how energy is supplied to, used by and lost in US manufacturing, from fuels, electricity and steam through end uses such as boilers, process heaters, HVAC and machine drives, together with combustion and process greenhouse gas emissions. There are 21 footprints: 15 manufacturing sectors, 5 subsectors and all manufacturing, together covering 95% of the primary energy used by US manufacturing. They are produced by the U.S. Department of Energy's Industrial Efficiency and Decarbonization Office from the 2018 Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey of the Energy Information Administration, EPA emissions inventory data and industry expert input, and were published in December 2021; versions for 2006, 2010 and 2014 remain available. The footprints and guides to definitions, scope and assumptions are free PDF files. Caveats: the reference year is 2018, the diagrams are PDF graphics, not machine-readable tables, and loss estimates rely on assumptions. For simulation they give energy demand by end use and sector for capacity planning and resilience studies, for example estimating how gas or power outages would hit different manufacturing sectors. It is related to the US Census Annual Survey of Manufactures record in this catalogue, which gives the economic side of the same sectors.
